newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU finds Boeing deal lacking, EU source says.
newsitem.headline: EU finds Boeing deal lacking, EU source says.

text.p: European Union competition experts agreed Friday that the proposed merger between Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp should be blocked if the aerospace companies do not make changes to meet the EU's antitrust concerns, an EU source said Friday.
"If adequate remedies are not offered, the proposed concentration should be prohibited," the source said, quoting from a finding from the experts to be issued later.

The European Union must approve any corporate mergers, even those outside European borders, if the companies involved do business in member countries and their combination is seen as possibly affecting competition in the bloc.
European critics of the Boeing-McDonnell deal say it will create an unfair competitor to Europe's Airbus consortium in the market for commercial jetliners.
Competition experts from all 15 EU member states met in Brussels on Friday to discuss the $14 billion merger.
Sources said they unanimously agreed that the merger would create a dominant position and should be prohibited.
The sources said the experts had also agreed that offers made so far by Boeing to seal the deal under EU law were "not sufficient to prevent such a strengthening of dominant position."
They said the Commission was planning to continue talking to Boeing to see whether "adequate remedies" would be forthcoming.
